overview: This 145-page file traces Japan’s postwar petroleum policy from 1946 to 1949. State Department, occupation, and oil-company records document disputes over the Petroleum Distribution Kodan and foreign-owned facilities, domestic production policy, tanker voyages to the Persian Gulf, and the return of distribution and refining to private operation. Statistics, directives, and reports show how supply and infrastructure were rebuilt.
interest: Shows competing company and occupation priorities through policy correspondence, operating directives, tanker negotiations, and production statistics.
